room.prompt: Create one cinematic production SET REFERENCE photograph of the modern newlywed bedroom for the original Chinese romantic comedy 她头顶有弹幕. The room is EMPTY: no people, no faces, no text, no logos. Wide horizontal composition, live-action photographic realism, refined but lived-in modern interior, warm walnut wood, ivory and taupe fabrics, soft amber practical light with dark blue night outside. Spatial layout MUST be very legible and will remain fixed in subsequent storyboards: viewed from the entrance/front of the room, the king-size bed and low upholstered headboard occupy the BACK LEFT, a dark night window with partially closed taupe curtains is at BACK CENTER, a modest two-seat warm-gray sofa runs along the RIGHT WALL, and a small rectangular walnut writing table sits in the CENTER FOREGROUND with two chairs facing each other across its short left and right ends. Keep a clear path from the right-hand chair to the sofa. The two people will later sit woman at screen LEFT facing right and man at screen RIGHT facing left. On the low ottoman near the RIGHT side of the bed is ONE distinct spare ivory sleeping pillow that can be carried to the sofa. There are also normal pillows on the bed; the sofa initially has NO sleeping pillow. On the writing table, near the right chair, place a plain cream sheet of paper, a simple black pen, and a SMALL PALE GREEN JADE oval pendant with a worn muted red cord; details must be subtle and realistic, no glowing in this reference, no readable writing. The desk should be intimate rather than huge, people can face each other comfortably less than two meters apart. No giant chandeliers, no ornate palatial furniture, no red wedding banners, no flowers blocking sightlines. Soft key light from screen-left, subtle cool window fill, graceful uncluttered composition with enough real furnishings to identify this SAME room in close-ups. Camera eye level at about seated head height, 28-35mm lens impression, not an extreme fisheye. Prioritize a coherent fixed bedroom floor plan and clear bed-table-sofa relationship. Compose as a wide 16:9 film establishing shot.

boards.prompt:
Use the attached approved FEMALE and MALE casting sheets as exact fictional character identity references, and the attached bedroom photograph as the fixed set reference. Create a professional SIX-PANEL COLOR FILM STORYBOARD CONTACT SHEET for episode 1 入职第一天 of the contemporary Chinese romantic comedy 她头顶有弹幕. EXACTLY SIX separately bordered horizontal 16:9 cinematic panels in reading order, arranged THREE COLUMNS by TWO ROWS on a warm ivory page. Each film panel must be WIDE, not square or vertical. Generous clean gutters and short captions under panels. Overall sheet landscape 3:2 with room for title, captions and breathing room. Photorealistic live-action film stills, consistent realistic skin, warm amber bedroom lighting and soft dark-blue night window fill, NOT sketches, NOT anime. The SAME woman 温书窈 appears in every female shot: age26, oval face and dark expressive eyes matching first sheet, tiny beauty mark below her LEFT eye, dark low chignon, pearl drop earrings, dusty-blush LONG SLEEVE silk V-neck midi dress. SAME man 沈既白 in every male shot: age29, exact facial features and black hair matching second sheet, charcoal suit white shirt solid navy tie, no beard. Keep their identities and outfits fixed; do not beautify into different actors. Fixed staging: woman seated SCREEN LEFT looking RIGHT, man seated SCREEN RIGHT looking LEFT during dialogue. Bed stays BACK LEFT, dark window BACK CENTER, warm-gray sofa RIGHT WALL; walnut table and two chairs in foreground, cream paper black pen and small pale jade pendant with red cord on tabletop. Spare ivory sleeping pillow starts on bed-foot ottoman until shot21. No extra people or duplicated bodies. Close-ups must genuinely change framing as described, NOT repeat the same portrait six times. No speech balloons, thought text, subtitles, floating words or readable handwriting inside movie panels: we add these later. Leave appropriate headroom above woman in thought shots. Put ONLY the specified shot number, time span and short Chinese shot label BELOW each panel, not over the actors. Upper header has project title, episode title and PAGE number; lower footer '16:9 横屏 · 静帧分镜 · 时间为剪辑预算'. All labels sparse and legible. Each panel is exactly the single keyframe described, not a nested collage.

Panel 4: Closer male-POV shot of the woman with lips clearly CLOSED and impeccably polite expression, eye contact slightly to screen right. Generous uncluttered space above her head for later thoughts, but absolutely NO text inside image.
